QF.id: XIII Introduction to Forwards and Futures_48

question.text: What is the difference between 'initial margin' and 'maintenance margin' in futures trading?

answer.text: Initial margin is the upfront deposit required to open a position; maintenance margin is the minimum level below which the account cannot fall — if it does, a margin call requires the trader to restore it to initial margin level
Initial margin is higher and is paid once; maintenance margin is a daily fee for holding the position
Initial margin is for long positions; maintenance margin is for short positions
They are the same — both refer to the minimum required deposit

explanation.text: The Logic: Initial margin is the upfront deposit required to open a futures position. Maintenance margin is a lower threshold — set as a defined fraction of initial margin — below which the account balance cannot fall. If daily mark-to-market losses pull the account equity below the maintenance level, a margin call is triggered and the trader must top the account back up to the initial-margin level before continuing. The Trap: Maintenance margin is not a daily fee — it is a trigger level. It is not specific to long or short positions; both face the same MTM and margin mechanics. And initial and maintenance margin are different amounts (initial is larger). Note: The NISM Series VIII (Equity Derivatives), Series I (Currency Derivatives), and Series IV (Interest Rate Derivatives) workbook pages reviewed describe initial margin, daily MTM, and the SPAN/ELM framework used in India, but do not specifically define maintenance margin as a 75-80% threshold or describe a restore-to-initial-margin call in those terms. The framing above is presented as general futures-market industry knowledge rather than a workbook citation.
